record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.original_question: For bipartite quantum states, a state is distillable if sufficiently many copies can be converted by local quantum operations and classical communication into an approximation of a maximally entangled singlet state. States with positive partial transpose are known not to be distillable. Is the converse true: must every undistillable bipartite state have positive partial transpose?

evidence.quote: A state on a bipartite quantum system is called distillable, if from sufficiently many pairs prepared in that state one can obtain a close approximation of a maximally entangled singlet state, using only local quantum operations and classical communication (LOCC). It is well-known that states with positive partial transpose (PPT) are not distillable. The problem is to decide the converse.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider bipartite quantum systems with finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_A\otimes\mathcal{H}_B$. A state $\rho$ on this system is a positive semidefinite trace-one operator. The partial transpose $\rho^{T_B}$ is defined by transposing the second tensor factor in some product basis; $\rho$ is said to have positive partial transpose (PPT) if $\rho^{T_B}\geq 0$, and otherwise to have non-positive partial transpose (NPT). 

The state $\rho$ is called distillable if there exists an integer $n\geq 1$ such that, by applying local quantum operations and classical communication (LOCC) to $\rho^{\otimes n}$, one can produce a state arbitrarily close (in trace norm) to a two-qubit maximally entangled singlet state $|\psi^-\rangle\langle\psi^-|$ on a chosen pair of qubits embedded in the local systems. Equivalently, $\rho$ is distillable iff there exist $n$ and a Schmidt rank-2 vector $|\phi\rangle$ such that $\langle\phi|(\rho^{\otimes n})^{T_B}|\phi\rangle<0$.

It is known that every PPT state is undistillable. Determine whether the converse holds: is every undistillable bipartite state PPT? Equivalently, does there exist an NPT state that is undistillable (NPT bound entanglement)?
artifact.status_search_result: The NPT bound entanglement / distillability problem remains a well-known open problem in quantum information theory. Recent work in 2024 (e.g., a Phys. Rev. A paper and arXiv:2402.18037) explicitly states the equivalence between PPT entanglement and bound entanglement is a long-standing open problem and proposes partial approaches, with only limited progress even for Werner states.

status_evidence.title: Unveiling NPT bound problem: From Distillability Sets to Inequalities and Multivariable Insights
status_evidence.snippet: The equivalence between PPT entanglement and bound entanglement is a long-standing open problem in quantum information theory. Limited progress has been made so far.

status_evidence.title: Nonpositive-transpose entanglement and bound entanglement (Phys. Rev. A 110, 012406)
status_evidence.snippet: Long-standing open problem; proposes new decomposition and multivariable approach.
status_evidence.claim: Recent peer-reviewed work confirms the problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: Bipartite bound entanglement
status_evidence.snippet: Whether bipartite NPT states can be distilled is a long-standing open problem, listed among five open problems in quantum information theory.
status_evidence.claim: Listed as open in 2024 survey-style work.
